title: Three leftover disputes: infants' actual faith, how far baptism is necessary, and whether the Spirit's baptism is tied to the water
pass_a_gloss: Such is the Controversy, 1. About the actual faith of Infants: whom the Reformed judge a subject capable of faith as to its principle, seed, root, habit, infused by God in a manner incomprehensible to us; and so capable of some grace, even inward, such as federal grace is — namely, taken up with their parents into the Covenant and sharers of the promise (Acts 2:39). So also capable of sacramental sanctification, as by Circumcision (Romans 4:11), so by Baptism (1 Corinthians 7:14; Colossians 2:14). Finally capable of the remission of original sin and of justifying grace. 2. Such also is the Controversy about a certain degree of the necessity of holy Baptism; whence according to them, from mere deprivation, apart from any voluntary neglect, there arises either deprivation of salvation, or at least danger of it. 3. Such also about the mode of efficacy; that to the ceremony of Baptism the grace of Regeneration is bound, or (as they say) to the baptism of water is bound the baptism of the Spirit/flame, as its effect, but (as they add) ordinarily; and yet not from the opus operatum of the Papists, but by the operation of the Holy Spirit.
pass_b_english: The leftover controversy runs like this. First, about infants' actual faith. The Reformed take them as able to receive faith in its principle, seed, root, and habit — poured in by God in a way we cannot grasp — and so able to receive some grace, even inward grace: federal grace, as children taken with their parents into the covenant and sharers of the promise (Acts 2:39).

So they are capable of sacramental sanctification, as by circumcision (Romans 4:11), so by baptism (1 Corinthians 7:14; Colossians 2:14); and finally capable of the remission of original sin and of justifying grace.
Second, about how far holy baptism is necessary. On their side, bare lack of it — with no willful neglect — already works either loss of salvation, or at least danger of that loss.

Third, about the mode of efficacy: that regenerating grace is bound to the baptismal ceremony, or (in their phrase) the baptism of the Spirit is bound to the baptism of water as its effect — ordinarily, they add — yet not by the Papists' opus operatum, but by the Holy Spirit's own working.
source_text: Talis est Controversia, 1. Circa fidem actualem Infantum: Quos Reformati censent subjectum capax fidei, quoad hujus principium, semen, radicem, habitum, modo nobis ἀκαταλήπτῳ divinitus infusum; Capaces adeo esse gratiae alicujus, etiam internae, uti sunt gratiae foederalis, scil. cum parentibus assumpti in Foedus, & participes promissionis, Act. II.39. Sic capaces sanctificationis Sacramentalis, uti per Circumcisionem, Rom. IV.11. ita per Baptismum 1. Cor. VII.14. Col. II.14. Denique capaces remissionis peccati Original. & gratiae justificantis. 2. Talis quoque Controversia, circa gradum quendam necessitatis S. Baptismi; Unde secundum illos, ex sola privatione, citra neglectum ullum voluntarium, oriatur aut privatio salutis, aut periculum saltem hujus. 3. Talis & circa efficaciae modum; Ut Ceremoniae Baptismi sit alligata gratia Regenerationis, vel (ut loquuntur) Baptismo fluminis alligatus Baptismus flaminis, tanquam illius effectus, sed (ut addunt) ordinariè; neque tamen ex opere operato Pontificiorum, sed operatione Spiritus S.

lemmas.gloss: baptism of water / of the Spirit (flame)
the work as performed (ex opere operato)

notes: Controv. print pp. 67-68 / PDF ~168-169. Controversies 1-3: actual faith of infants; degree of necessity from bare privation; mode of efficacy (Baptismus fluminis / flaminis; not ex opere operato).

Greek retained for infused infant-faith mode; Pass B says we cannot grasp
